Issue 3872: SV_ShadingRate is accepted in hull and domain shader control-point
signatures. The complaint is that DXC says nothing, so what you are looking for
is an ABSENCE -- and an absence is only readable next to a control.

This one file feeds five panes. Two compile positions the report says should be
rejected; two are controls that put the same semantic, in the same stage, with
the same compiler, into a position the interpretation table already marks NA.

  1. dxc_trunk  -T ds_6_4 -E DSOutMain   the domain shader WRITES the rate.
     ACCEPTED. Scroll to "Output signature" and read the SysValue column of the
     SV_ShadingRate row: it says SHDINGRATE, so this was lowered as a system
     value, not quietly demoted to an arbitrary semantic. The D3D12 Variable
     Rate Shading spec says the rate may be set from VS, GS or MS and "It is
     not permitted from other stages, for example DS".
  2. dxc_trunk  -T ds_6_4 -E DSInBad     CONTROL, same compiler, same stage:
     "Semantic SV_ShadingRate is invalid for shader model: ds". So the check
     exists and these command lines reach it. Pane 1's silence is a decision
     recorded in a table, not a check that never ran.
  3. dxc_trunk  -T hs_6_4 -E HSCPInMain  hull shader input control point.
     ACCEPTED, same reading as pane 1 but in "Input signature".
  4. dxc_trunk  -T hs_6_4 -E HSPCOutBad  CONTROL for the hull stage.
  5. dxc 1.6.2112  -T ds_6_4 -E DSOutMain   the release closest to the report
     date. Same result: this is not a recent regression. Locally it also
     reproduces on every release from 1.4.1907 onward.

Not shown, and why: the DXIL validator does not catch it either -- dxv accepts
all four containers, and both gates read the same SemanticInterpretation table.
Clang trunk cannot be asked this question yet; it rejects the name outright with
"unknown HLSL semantic". FXC rejects it too, but it rejects it in the vertex
shader as well, because the feature postdates Shader Model 5.1.
